title: Failure Fingerprint Catalog + Error Burst Explorer (trace/metric/log enrichment)
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: We currently have many dashboards that show raw error counts and SLI breaches, but it is hard to quickly group related incidents that share the same root cause across traces, metrics, and logs. This ticket introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) a canonical Failure Fingerprint Catalog (FFC) produced by trace hook enrichment + log/metric pipelines, and (2) an interactive Error Burst Explorer dashboard to surface temporal bursts of the same fingerprint so on-call and incident response can prioritize and remediate faster.

Goals:
- Define and implement a compact, deterministic failure fingerprint schema that captures the minimal attributes necessary to group like-for-like failures (service, route, transport code, model_error_class, queue_depth_bucket, scheduling_latency_bucket).
- Add a trace hook to compute and attach failure.fingerprint and failure.tags to spans at the point of error detection (model runtime exceptions, timeout, requeue, backpressure).
- Enrich logs and metrics pipelines (log-forwarder and metrics-aggregation) to preserve failure.fingerprint and add dedicated metrics series for burst detection.
- Build Error Burst Explorer in Console: time-to-first-burst, burst duration, top fingerprints, drilldown to example traces and sample logs, annotation of autoscale/failover events.
- Ensure low cardinality of fingerprints (< 2500 active daily) and a fallback hashing strategy for unknown fields.

Non-goals: full-stack RCA automation, automatic remediation, or replacing existing dashboards overnight.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical fingerprint schema doc exists in Confluence and is approved by Observability and Runtime leads.
Trace hook: spans with error states include failure.fingerprint and failure.tags (string and array) for synchronous and async model calls.
Log pipeline preserves failure.fingerprint for all application logs and emits a daily exported table for analytics (bigquery path).
A new Console dashboard ‘Error Burst Explorer’ is live in staging with: burst detection algorithm (rolling z-score), list of top-20 fingerprints, and trace/log drilldown links.
Burst alert rule created (P0 on-call) that groups by fingerprint with configurable sensitivity, tested in staging.
Fingerprint cardinality stays below target on a 2-week rolling window; if exceeded, the system falls back to hashed short fingerprint and emits a cardinality-increase alert.
technical_design: Fingerprint schema (RFC): failure.fingerprint := join(':', service, route, transport_code, model_error_class|'none', queue_depth_bucket, sched_latency_bucket). Example: 'runtime:generate:v1:HTTP_504:MODEL_TIMEOUT:Q3:L2'.
Compute model_error_class using runtime error classifier: {ModelTimeout, ModelOOM, TokenizationError, GenerationDivergence, BadRequest}. Fall back to 'unknown'.
Queue depth buckets: Q0(0-2), Q1(3-8), Q2(9-32), Q3(33+). Scheduling latency buckets: L0(<2ms), L1(2-10ms), L2(10-50ms), L3(50ms+).

Trace hook implementation: runtime agent (C++) will call span->SetTag('failure.fingerprint', fingerprint) and span->SetTag('failure.tags', csv_tags). Java/Python SDKs will mirror extraction for client-side errors.
Log enrichment: log-forwarder pipeline (fluentd/collector) will copy trace tags into structured log fields 'failure.fingerprint' and 'failure.tags' and route to BigQuery/ELK retention index.

Metric generation: a new counter metric 'rwd.failure.fingerprint.count' with label 'fingerprint' emitted at 1m resolution; a derived series 'rwd.failure.fingerprint.burst' computed using rolling z-score over 15m windows in the metrics pipeline for dashboard signals.

Burst detection algorithm: compute z = (current_rate - mean(window)) / stddev(window); mark burst when z > 4 for at least 3 consecutive minutes OR rate > baseline * 5. Both thresholds configurable in Console.

Backpressure signals: include 'gpu_util_bucket', 'pending_kv_cache_ops' as additional tags for internal drilling but not part of canonical fingerprint unless explicitly enabled via sampling to keep cardinality low.

Cardinality control: canonical fingerprint uses only bounded enums; unknown string fields are hashed to 8-char summary when necessary. A daily job summarizes active distinct fingerprints and sends an alert if >2500.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): implement RFC and unit tests; deploy trace hook to runtime dev images; add local simulator to generate fingerprints.

Phase 1 (staging): enable trace tag propagation and log enrichment for staging; populate BigQuery; ship initial Error Burst Explorer in staging Console behind feature flag; test burst alerts with synthetic workloads.
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 10% of traffic in prod (split by customer tier) for 48h; monitor fingerprint cardinality and alert noisiness.
Phase 3 (prod): global rollout with gradual increase and dashboard public; run 2-week observability post-launch review and tune burst thresholds.
Rollback: if cardinality explosion or alert noise > 10x, revert enrichment layer and fallback to hashed fingerprint; pause burst alerts.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Ava Martinez: Drafted RFC and initial schema. Left notes about potential explosion if we include model_version; proposing sampling for model_version only.
2025-02-13 - Ravi Patel: Implemented C++ trace hook prototype; added SetTag for failure.fingerprint and started unit tests. PR opened: runtime#1209.

2025-02-15 - Priya Desai (Observability): Reviewed RFC. Suggests adding rolling z-score burst detection and a secondary heuristic for absolute rate to reduce false positives during release traffic spikes.
2025-02-17 - Ravi Patel: Wire up log-forwarder mapping and BigQuery export path. Found that fluentd plugin dropped tags when logs were multiline; added YAML fix and test.
2025-02-19 - On-call rotation: Ran synthetic bursts in staging; detected burst for fingerprint 'runtime:generate:v1:MODEL_TIMEOUT:Q3:L3' and validated trace drilldown links resolve to span ids.
2025-02-20 - Security review (Sophie Kline): Confirmed no PII is added by fingerprint. Request: ensure hashed fallback is irreversible and documented.
notes: We should consider aligning fingerprints with incident playbooks so on-call runbooks can surface remediation steps directly from fingerprint metadata.
Future work: allow customers to opt-in to higher-fidelity fingerprints that include model_version and request_seed for deeper triage (via tenant-level feature flag).
Measured KPI: time-to-ack for bursts should drop by 30% and mean time to remediate for fingerprinted incidents should drop by 20% in the 4 weeks after launch.
